rollback: If migration fails, keep backend/scheduler stopped and inspect SHOW COLUMNS/SHOW INDEX plus script statement results. Whole-script retry is unsafe because ADD COLUMN is not idempotent and MySQL DDL cannot be rolled back as one transaction.

Rollback of the full upgrade requires restoring the verified pre-upgrade backup into a clean replacement database, validating baseline counts/history there, pointing DB_URL at it and starting the previous code. Do not blindly import over the modified database or merely drop the new columns: cancellation updates are not reversed and new-version task history can conflict with the old unique key. Any writes accepted after restart would be lost by restoring the old backup; preserve them for review before choosing restore.
